text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Majority in parliament puts brake on deregulation of bus services. (p1)
- Accountants Coopers & Lybrand express concern about the number and calibre of business economics students. (p1)
- Property holding company Air Holding dismantles anti-takeover device. (p3)
- Brewer Heineken's depot in Kinsangani, Zaire was pillaged last weekend. (p3)
- Heineken signs letter ot intent to buy 51 pct stake in Israeli brewer Tempo. (p3)
- Cable maker Twentsche Kabel forecasts higher earnings in 1997, after posting 14 percent profit growth in 1996. (p4)
- Royal Dutch/Shell meets Amnesty International's criticism halfway in revised general code of conduct. (p4)
- Computer company Tulip reports Dfl 9.95 million net loss in 1996, but is optimistic about 1997. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- The Netherlands will be almost completely urbanised in ten years. (p1)
- Pig farmers forced to claim income support as swine fever outbreak slashes income. (p1)
- Cabinet to invest in educational infrastructure, increase teachers' salaries, overhaul primary and secondary education. (p3)
- Amsterdam Exchanges' shares to be priced at 1,400-1,800 guilders. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Paid parking in Dutch city centres leads to reduction in retailers' turnover. (p1)
- The Dutch ate 4.5 kilos of chocolate per head in 1996. (p3)
- Dutch guilder is losing ground against the D-Mark. (p23)
- Dutch measuring institute NHI to open a branch office in Brazil. (p27)
TROUW
- Shell's code of conduct harvests praise and scepticism. (p1)
- Advertising code commission RCC rules that Pepsi Cola's ad for "Maxer" is misleading. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- European finance ministers oppose Dutch plans for ecotax on energy. (p1)
